fixture_encoding.status: [INFERENCE] Recipes only; no fixture files created by this seat.
fixture_encoding.header: Four literal bytes 47 47 55 46, then endian-specific uint32 version, uint64 tensor_count, uint64 kv_count; metadata begins at byte 24.
fixture_encoding.string: Endian-specific uint64 UTF-8 byte length followed by exactly those bytes, with no NUL terminator.
fixture_encoding.kv: GGUF string key, uint32 type tag, typed value; no padding between KVs or array elements.
fixture_encoding.array: uint32 element_type, uint64 element_count, then that many values. STRING elements each retain their own uint64 byte length.
fixture_encoding.ordinary_fixture_completion: Use tensor_count=0; for complete-container positive oracle fixtures, pad after metadata to the explicit general.alignment (or 32 when absent). Never add padding inside a deliberately truncated value.

R_BASE.model_sha256_post: SHA256 of the exact generated GGUF fixture, using independent hashlib over all file bytes

model.sha256: same full-file digest unless a case overrides it

R_BASE.scope: Minimal synthetic reconciliation input, not a live receipt or receipt-gate validity assertion.

fixture_encoding.materialization_bounds: Every proposed new fixture fits within 1 MiB. Huge lengths/counts are encoded in their fixed-width fields, never materialized as huge arrays or files. The real 1,185,376-byte model is an existing external input, not copied into this output directory.

detector_contract.status: [INFERENCE] Detector design only; no detector command was run or is presented as executed.
detector_contract.observation: For positive parsing cases, require completed decoded JSON and compare version, endianness, counts, selected keys and array summaries to committed independent expectations. For malformed parser cases, match the named DecodeError outcome, its exact public stderr reason and exit, not exit alone. For reconciliation compare returned status/exit_code, digest binding, numeric context fields and classification; explicitly catch only ReceiptReconciliationError for malformed-receipt expectations.
detector_contract.positive_oracle: Generate small complete positive containers independently of the subject's fixture/pack_value helpers; use pinned official gguf.GGUFReader and ReaderField.contents to freeze expected values before mutation. Do not use the subject's output as its own oracle.
detector_contract.negative_oracle: Use explicit wire-format facts or declared lane-bound policy as indicated per mutant. Do not assume every malformed case is rejected by every official reader. Never call the full official reader on a huge declared count just to establish an expected bounded rejection.
three_arms: In one isolated disposable copy, save and hash pristine subject bytes and freeze detector/fixtures/oracle records.
Run the exact same selected bounded detector on pristine bytes; any baseline failure is inconclusive.
Apply exactly the single behavior change named by that mutant and run the unchanged detector.
Restore exact pristine bytes in a finally path even after detector failure; compare restoration hash to the saved pristine hash, then run the unchanged detector on restored bytes.
detector_contract.killed: Only after pristine and restored expectations pass: a completed, identified subject outcome contradicts a frozen expected value, acceptance/rejection, identity verdict or context classification.
detector_contract.survived: The selected detector completes and the identified mutated outcome still satisfies its frozen expectations. Record a coverage finding or a redundant/equivalent mutation; never weaken the contract to manufacture a kill.
detector_contract.inconclusive: Baseline/restoration failure, missing fixture/oracle, uncaught exception, silent nonzero, signal, timeout, early-abort selftest, malformed observation or missing selected case result. A matching target literal in crash output is not a kill.

existing_fixture_alignment.status: Peer-proposed names, not independently observed materialized fixture files at design time.
important_distinctions: Nonzero small counts catch cursor-width mistakes but not a preserving-offset uint32 truncation; M03/M04 include a high word.
The real receipt's ctx=served_n_ctx=256 does not kill source substitution; M22 deliberately separates them.
Slot multiply/divide, equality, array element-count and numeric-endian mutants require comparing decoded fields, not exit-only agreement.
A generated fixture is not a confirmed kill until its pristine baseline, mutant outcome and exact restored arm have actually been observed.
